original.target_description: The published Rasinski et al. (2005) study compares honesty-related with neutral words for four alcohol-related behaviors and cheating questions. It does not administer or report the BIDR impression-management subscale.

replication.target_description: Experiment 4 in online supplement, English-speaking Mechanical Turk participants from India; BIDR IM outcome. Main article identifies this study but does not print its target statistics.

reported_success.quote: None of the studies provided any evidence that honesty priming increases candor of responding.

notes:
Original full primary paper unavailable: DOI landing not accessible; CiteSeer PDF returned 404/timeout; Unpaywall and OpenAlex report no open-access location. Original statistics quoted secondarily in replication paper were not used. Supplied replication page locators appear to refer to a manuscript rather than the six-page published article. Supplement target statistics could not be independently acquired: publisher full-page fetch returned 429; publisher CDN supplement DOC and PDF routes returned 403 and were not retried. Main-paper narrative supports the reported failure, but no sample size, effect size or p value for the fourth study was substituted from other studies or sources.
Source follow-up: Published article title and DOI match the assigned original reference. Outcome mismatch: no BIDR IM test is reported, so the alcohol-composite sample and statistics are not substituted. Original only; replication and narrative replication success were not examined.
